## Books Company Settings

The company the books belong to (`company`, which is also `cardTitle`), and the view of the books' settings.

### Settings
The settings live in the realm's configuration, the `config` object in its `realm.json`, because that is what a card operation can read (`realmConfig()`). The Ledger reaches the same object through `settings`, a link to the realm's config card, and shows each one. Every setting is optional; an unset one has the default shown. A setting that is set but malformed shows on the Ledger as what is wrong with it, since the operations enforce the raw value.

| Key | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `closedThrough` | `yyyy-mm-dd`; nothing dated on or before it posts | none: any date posts |
| `materiality` | integer cents; a journal entry at or above it needs a reviewer | none |
| `chart` | the account codes (text) a document may post to | any code |
| `currency` | ISO 4217 home currency | `USD` |
| `fiscalYearStart` | month the fiscal year starts, 1–12 | `1` |
| `multicurrency` | `true` lets an invoice, bill or payment post in another currency | `false` |
| `currencies` | ISO 4217 codes a document may use besides the home currency | none |

`closedThrough`, `currency` and `fiscalYearStart` are computed on the card from these. `accounts` lists the account cards, so the Ledger can flag chart codes that have no account card, and account cards whose code isn't in the chart. `booksSettings()` in `ledger-settings.gts` reads a config object into typed settings with these defaults. The balance sheet, budget against actuals, the P&L forecast and the year close link to the same settings for the fiscal year start.

```json
"config": { "closedThrough": "2026-12-31", "materiality": 2500000, "currency": "USD", "fiscalYearStart": 1, "chart": ["1000", "1100"] }
```

### Operations
The document ones create a draft with `status: draft` and `enteredBy` stamped with the acting user. None of them checks anything (a create can't assert); the document's own `post` does the checking.

- `enterBill` → Bill (also sets `paidMinor` to 0); `enterPayment` → Bill Payment; `enterDeposit` → Deposit.
- `enterRoast` → Roast Batch; `enterFulfillment` → Fulfillment; `enterCount` → Count Adjustment; `enterLanded` → Landed Cost.
- `enterPayroll` → Payroll Run; `enterBankPayment` → Bank Payment; `enterTransfer` → Transfer; `enterCardCharge` → Card Charge; `enterLoanPayment` → Loan Payment; `enterDisposal` → Asset Disposal; `enterVendorCredit` → Vendor Credit.
- `enterBankImport` → Bank Statement Import, stamping `importedBy`; `enterBankLine` → Bank Transaction, for review, with no stamp: it's the bank's record, not anyone's entry. The desk sends one of the first and one of the second per new line in a single batch.
- `enterJournal` → Journal Entry; `enterScheduled` → Scheduled Entry; `enterDepreciation` → Depreciation Run.

```ts
import { Ledger } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/accounting/ledger-cards';
```

Customer-side documents (invoices, sales receipts, customer payments) are entered from the Ledger Customer card instead.

### Non-goals
Holds no balances and posts nothing itself. Doesn't store the settings: change them in `realm.json`. A document in another currency formats its own amounts in that currency. Home-currency amounts in registers and reports format as USD for now, whatever `currency` says.

`taxCodes` in the settings holds each tax code's rates, which the sales' operations check against; the Ledger names any code whose rates differ from its TaxCode card.

### Example
`Ledger/cinder`, a coffee roaster's books. In a realm with no `config` it shows every default.
